scope: All challenge executables under test_problem except PHP; loaders and bundled libraries are not separate challenge cases.
method: Independent manual review of decompiled pseudocode, normalized Ctree statements, call sites, control flow, stack offsets, and caller constraints. Existing plugin findings were not used as labels.

unit.root: One independently triggerable vulnerability root. Repeated equivalent call sites are grouped.
unit.site: A concrete instruction/call site belonging to a root.
unit.excluded: Pure denial of service, resource leaks, and weak hardening without a dependable pwn primitive are excluded.

roots.evidence: Attacker bytes reach the bundled ISO-2022-CN-EXT converter; its escape-sequence emission can write past the supplied output end.
iconv does not append a terminator. strlen can read past the conversion buffer, and the resulting length is copied into the smaller original chunk.
Decrypted attacker-controlled plaintext is passed directly as printf's format argument.
The JSON length field controls memcpy independently of the actual message-string allocation length.
The global chunk pointer and size remain live after free and can be viewed, modified, or freed again.
The modify length is not checked against either the stored chunk size or the source message length.
The query-delimited path is copied with strncpy without writing a terminator, then consumed by string/file APIs.
Parsed Content-Length controls the second recv into the fixed per-socket 4096-byte request storage without a capacity check.
Each site dereferences chunk metadata immediately after sub_177F releases the freshly allocated chunk.
The delete action releases unk_50C0[index] through sub_177F but clears only the separate size array; show and repeated delete retain access to the dangling pointer slot.
free leaves qword_202060[index] non-null, enabling inspect, engrave, and repeated release on freed storage.
An existing large slot is freed before replacement allocation; a negative requested size forces allocation failure and leaves the old global pointer and size intact.
size zero is accepted; malloc(0) can return non-null and n becomes a1-1, i.e. SIZE_MAX, before memcpy.
The show response passes an uninitialized EDX-derived length to send instead of the length recorded by sub_1C26.
The decrypted malloc buffer has exactly the network-supplied length and no appended NUL before strcmp.
A repeated SET in the same transaction raw-frees a refcounted value; CLONE aliases can retain and later use that allocation.
Delete frees the global slot without clearing its pointer or size, so Edit and Delete remain available.
MessagePack-controlled username and password lengths are copied into two 256-byte stack arrays without upper bounds.
